action: Adds a horizontal loop cut across the upper torso and slides it, in X-ray front view with other parts (Cube.001-.003) already modelled.
tool: Loop Cut and Slide (Ctrl R), Move
why: Add rows for the chest shape
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges on the vertical edges of the chest band, cuts=1

action: Checks the torso side profile in Right Orthographic, then deletes a vertex (key overlay 'X', 'Z') and views the torso in solid shading.
view: Right Orthographic X-ray, then User Orthographic solid
why: Clear the chest area before adding breast volume
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[v], context='VERTS')

action: Adds a low-poly UV sphere inside the body mesh (it mirrors to both sides) and turns Mirror Clipping off.
tool: Add > UV Sphere (in Edit Mode), Mirror modifier
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, solid with reference
why: Use a sphere as the breast shape; clipping off so it can leave the mirror plane
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere(bm, u_segments=8, v_segments=6, radius=r, matrix=Matrix.Translation(pos)); m.use_clip=False (segment counts not readable)

action: Deletes the back half of the sphere, scales the remaining dome to 0.874 and places it on the chest in Right Orthographic.
why: Breast is a 25-vertex dome sitting on the chest
reader_equivalent: bmesh: delete sphere verts with y > center.y; bmesh.ops.scale(..., vec=(0.874,)*3); translate to chest

action: Selects the dome with Select Linked (delimit Normal) and adjusts it in front view; then switches to wireframe through the Z pie and moves boundary verts.
tool: Select Linked (L / Ctrl L), shading pie (Z), Move
view: Front Orthographic solid, then User Orthographic wireframe
why: Position the dome and line up its border with torso edges before joining
reader_equivalent: select linked by island in bmesh (walk faces from a seed); move verts

action: Connects the dome into the torso: the dome border is now part of the chest faces and a new edge runs from the dome down the torso.
why: Merge the breast into the body as one surface
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.bridge_loops between dome border and a torso hole, or bmesh.ops.connect_verts for each cut

action: Checks the smoothed chest in Object Mode, then returns to Edit Mode and moves chest verts (Move X 0.017165 m).
view: User Orthographic, Object Mode smooth shaded then Edit Mode
why: Judge the breast silhouette with smooth shading
reader_equivalent: render a viewport snapshot after bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth(); then edit co

action: Moves chest verts (Move Y and Z 0.005443 m) and slides verts along edges with Vertex Slide (factor 0.355, Clamp on).
why: Even out the edge flow around the breast
reader_equivalent: v.co = v.co.lerp(neighbor.co, 0.355)

action: Shift-selects the under-breast edges, adds cuts there and slides verts again (b x2).
why: Define the crease under the breast
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.connect_verts(bm, verts=[a,b]) for each new edge

action: Dissolves extra edges between the breasts with Dissolve Edges (Dissolve Vertices on, Face Split off).
why: Remove unneeded loops to keep the mesh low-poly
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.dissolve_edges(bm, edges=sel, use_verts=True, use_face_split=False)

action: Extrudes the neck up from the top of the torso, moves it 0.031935 m in Z, rotates it -11.8 degrees in View orientation, with Mirror Clipping back on.
view: Right Orthographic, Edit Mode, X-ray with reference
why: Block the neck at the forward lean seen in the side view
reader_equivalent: extrude top ring; translate z+0.032; bmesh.ops.rotate about X by -11.8 deg

action: Slides collarbone/shoulder verts with Vertex Slide (factor 0.289) to tidy the neck base.
why: Even spacing around the neck and shoulders
reader_equivalent: v.co = v.co.lerp(target.co, 0.289)

action: Adds a new cube (Cube.007) as a separate object for the hand, with no modifiers, and moves it in Edit Mode.
why: Model the hand apart from the body, then join it later
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(location=hand_pos)

action: Flattens the cube into a palm slab and adds loop cuts along it to make four finger columns.
tool: Resize (S), Loop Cut and Slide (Ctrl R)
why: One column of faces per finger
reader_equivalent: scale cube to a flat box; bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges on the width edges, cuts=3

action: Moves a palm corner to taper it, then bevels the front edges with one segment.
why: Split each finger root so fingers can be extruded with gaps between them
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=edges, offset=0.00197, segments=1, profile=0.5, affect='EDGES')

action: Places the palm at the hand position beside the hip in Front Orthographic (Move X 0.039919 m) with four finger faces now extruded.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, solid with reference
why: Size and place the hand against the body reference
reader_equivalent: translate all hand verts so the palm sits at the reference hand position

action: Looking at the finger ends from the front, moves verts (G x2) to shape the finger cross-sections and selects one finger face at a time.
why: Give the knuckle row a slight arch
reader_equivalent: adjust co of finger-root verts

action: Extrudes the four finger faces out into long boxes and shift-selects/moves them.
why: Fingers as extruded boxes
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_discrete_faces(bm, faces=finger_faces); translate along palm direction

action: Scales the finger tip faces to 0.5128 to taper the fingers, then checks from below.
why: Thin finger tips
reader_equivalent: for each tip face: bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=(0.5128,)*3, space=Matrix.Translation(-face.calc_center_median()), verts=face.verts)

action: In Top Orthographic with X-ray, moves finger tips to set different finger lengths.
view: Top Orthographic, X-ray wireframe, Edit Mode
why: Middle finger longest, little finger shortest
reader_equivalent: translate each tip face along the finger axis by its own length

action: Moves finger tips (D -0.01872 m) and scales finger rows (0.7587, then 0.7449) to narrow the fingers in Top view.
why: Fingers thinner than the palm columns
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.scale per finger on finger verts with factor 0.76/0.74

action: Adds loop cuts across the fingers for knuckles.
why: Joint loops so the fingers can bend when rigged
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges on each finger's long edges, cuts=1 or 2

action: Scales the new finger loops (S x2) so each finger has two segment loops, then checks the hand beside the thigh in Object Mode.
view: Top Orthographic Edit Mode, then User Orthographic Object Mode
why: Shape finger joints and check scale against the body
reader_equivalent: scale knuckle rings; then compare hand bbox to body bbox

action: From the front, moves finger-end verts in Y (0.001963 m, then -0.002607 m) to give each finger a rounded section.
view: Right Orthographic then User Orthographic, solid, Edit Mode
why: Round the square finger sections
reader_equivalent: adjust co of the corner verts of each finger section

action: Scales loops along the fingers and the palm (S, Tab S), keeping four fingers and no thumb yet.
why: Taper fingers and palm
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.scale on selected rings

action: Shift-selects the knuckle loops after adding more cuts so each finger has three joint rings.
why: Joint rings at each finger knuckle
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(..., cuts=2) per joint, then scale the rings

action: In Object Mode, uses the right-click Object menu to Shade Smooth the hand, then adds a loop cut across the palm (Edge Slide 0.3160).
tool: Object > Shade Smooth (W menu), Loop Cut and Slide (Ctrl R)
view: User Orthographic, Object Mode then Edit Mode, solid
why: Smooth look and an extra palm loop for thumb placement
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth(); bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges across the palm

action: Uses the Knife tool on the palm side to cut new edges where the thumb will come out.

settings.status_bar_tool: Cut, Close, Stop, Confirm, Cancel, Undo, Midpoint Snap, Ignore Snap, Cut Through, X-Ray, Angle Constraint

why: Make a face at the thumb base
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.connect_verts(bm, verts=[a,b]) for each knife cut

action: Selects the thumb-base face on the palm side and extrudes it out (Move X 0.024978, Y -0.003142, Z -0.002637 m).
why: Start the thumb from the side of the palm
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_face_region(bm, geom=[thumb_face]); translate (0.025,-0.003,-0.0026)

action: Rotates the thumb extrusion -13.74 degrees in Right Orthographic so it angles toward the palm.
why: Thumb points across the palm
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.rotate(bm, verts=thumb_verts, cent=base_center, matrix=Matrix.Rotation(radians(-13.74),3,'X'))

action: Extrudes the thumb further, scales its tip (S 1 overlay) and nudges verts (Move 0.000081, -0.000985, 0.003155 m).
why: Thumb with two segments and a tapered tip
reader_equivalent: repeat extrude_face_region + translate + scale on the thumb tip face

action: Selects the whole hand (all 261 verts) to transform it as one piece.
why: Finished hand is 261 verts / 264 faces before joining
reader_equivalent: for v in bm.verts: v.select=True

action: Moves the hand to the end of the arm and scales it by 1.422 in Front Orthographic.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, solid with reference
why: Fit hand size and position to the reference
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=(1.422,)*3, space=..., verts=bm.verts); translate to wrist

action: Joins the hand object into the mirrored body mesh 'Cube' (Ctrl J), so the Mirror modifier makes the second hand.

settings.status_bar: Collection | Cube | Verts 2,950 | Faces 2,780 | Tris 5,402 | Objects 1/9

why: One body mesh; the left hand comes from the mirror
reader_equivalent: select hand and body, set body active; bpy.ops.object.join() (needs a context with both selected)

action: Saves the file (Ctrl S, 'Saved female_char1.blend').
why: Checkpoint after the body and hands
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
